o: Cómo Lázaro se asentó con un escudero, y de lo que le acaeció con él.
t: How Lazarillo settled in with a squire, and what befell him at his hands.

o: Desta manera me fue forzado sacar fuerzas de flaqueza y, poco a poco, con ayuda de las buenas gentes di comigo en esta insigne ciudad de Toledo, adonde con la merced de Dios dende a quince días se me cerró la herida; y mientras estaba malo, siempre me daban alguna limosna, mas después que estuve sano, todos me decían.
t: In this way I was forced to gather strength from weakness, and little by little, with the help of good folk, I found myself in this noble city of Toledo, where, God be thanked, fifteen days later my wound closed; and while I was ill they always gave me some alms, but once I was well again, everyone said to me:

o: "Tú, bellaco y gallofero eres.
t: "You are a rogue and a cheat.

o: Busca, busca un amo a quien sirvas."
t: Go and find, go and find a master to serve."

o: "¿Y adónde se hallará ése -decía yo entre mí- si Dios agora de nuevo, como crió el mundo, no le criase?
t: "And where will this one be found," I said to myself, "if God now, as He created the world, should not create him?"

o: Andando así discurriendo de puerta en puerta, con harto poco remedio, porque ya la caridad se subió al cielo, topóme Dios con un escudero que iba por la calle con razonable vestido, bien peinado, su paso y compás en orden.
t: Thus, wandering from door to door, with very little remedy, for charity had already gone up to heaven, God brought me face to face with a squire who was going down the street decently dressed, well groomed, his step and his bearing in order.

o: Miróme, y yo a él, y díjome.
t: He looked at me, and I at him, and he said to me:

o: "Mochacho, ¿buscas amo?"
t: "Lad, are you looking for a master?"

o: Yo le dije: "Sí, señor."
t: I said to him: "Yes, sir."

o: "Pues vente tras mí -me respondió- que Dios te ha hecho merced en topar comigo.
t: "Well, come along behind me," he answered, "for God has done you a kindness in setting you in my way.

o: Alguna buena oración rezaste hoy."
t: Some good prayer must you have said today."

o: Y seguíle, dando gracias a Dios por lo que le oí, y también que me parecía, según su hábito y continente, ser el que yo había menester.
t: And I followed him, giving thanks to God for what I had heard, and also because it seemed to me, from his bearing and his manner, that he was the very man I needed.

o: Era de mañana cuando este mi tercero amo topé, y llevóme tras sí gran parte de la ciudad.
t: It was morning when I found this third master of mine, and he led me behind him through a good part of the city.

o: Pasábamos por las plazas do se vendía pan y otras provisiones.
t: We passed through the squares where bread and other provisions were sold.

o: Yo pensaba y aun deseaba que allí me quería cargar de lo que se vendía, porque ésta era propria hora cuando se suele proveer de lo necesario; mas muy a tendido paso pasaba por estas cosas.
t: I thought, and even wished, that he wanted to load up there on what was being sold, because that was the proper hour for provisioning oneself with what was needed; but he passed very quickly over these things.

o: "Por ventura no lo vee aquí a su contento -decía yo- y querrá que lo compremos en otro cabo."
t: "Perhaps he doesn't see it here to his liking," I said, "and he'll want us to buy it at some other point."

o: Desta manera anduvimos hasta que dio las once.
t: Thus we went on until it struck eleven.

o: Entonces se entró en la iglesia mayor, y yo tras él, y muy devotamente le vi oír misa y los otros oficios divinos, hasta que todo fue acabado y la gente ida.
t: Then he went into the cathedral, and I after him, and very devoutly I watched him hear Mass and the other divine offices, until it was all over and the people had gone.

o: Entonces salimos de la iglesia.
t: Then we left the church.

o: A buen paso tendido comenzamos a ir por una calle abajo.
t: Setting off at a good, steady pace, we began to go down a street.

o: Yo iba el más alegre del mundo en ver que no nos habíamos ocupado en buscar de comer.
t: I went as happy as could be, seeing that we had not troubled ourselves to look for anything to eat.

o: Bien consideré que debía ser hombre, mi nuevo amo, que se proveía en junto, y que ya la comida estaría a punto tal y como yo la deseaba y aun la había menester.
t: I considered well that my new master must be a man who provides for himself in bulk, and that the food would soon be ready just as I had wished it and had need of.

o: Desque fuimos entrados, quita de sobre sí su capa y, preguntando si tenía las manos limpias, la sacudimos y doblamos, y muy limpiamente soplando un poyo que allí estaba, la puso en él.
t: Once we had gone in, he took off his cloak and, asking whether I had clean hands, we shook it out and folded it, and, blowing it very clean on a bench that was there, he laid it on it.

o: Y hecho esto, sentóse cabo della, preguntándome muy por extenso de dónde era y cómo había venido a aquella ciudad; y yo le di más larga cuenta que quisiera, porque me parecía más conveniente hora de mandar poner la mesa y escudillar la olla que de lo que me pedía.
t: And having done this, he sat down beside it, asking me at great length where I was from and how I had come to that city; and I gave him a longer account than he wanted, because it seemed to me more convenient to have the table set and the pot scraped than to answer what he was asking me.

o: Con todo eso, yo le satisfice de mi persona lo mejor que mentir supe, diciendo mis bienes y callando lo demás, porque me parecía no ser para en cámara.
t: With all that, I satisfied him about my person as best I knew how to lie, telling him of my possessions and keeping silent about the rest, because it seemed to me I was not made for a chamber.

o: Esto hecho, estuvo ansí un poco, y yo luego vi mala señal, por ser ya casi las dos y no le ver más aliento de comer que a un muerto.
t: This done, he stayed like that a while, and I soon saw a bad sign, for it was already nearly two o'clock and I saw no more appetite for eating in him than in a dead man.

o: Después desto, consideraba aquel tener cerrada la puerta con llave ni sentir arriba ni abajo pasos de viva persona por la casa.
t: After this, that man considered having the door locked with a key and hearing no footsteps of any living person up or down the house.

o: Todo lo que yo había visto eran paredes, sin ver en ella silleta, ni tajo, ni banco, ni mesa, ni aun tal arcaz como el de marras: finalmente, ella parecía casa encantada.
t: All I had seen were walls, with no chair, no chopping block, no bench, no table, not even such a chest as the one of yore: in short, it seemed an enchanted house.

o: Estando así, díjome.
t: With that, he said to me.

o: "Tú, mozo, ¿has comido?"
t: "You, lad, have you eaten?"

o: "No, señor -dije yo-, que aún no eran dadas las ocho cuando con vuestra merced encontré."
t: "No, sir," I said, "it was not yet eight o'clock when I met your grace."

o: "Pues, aunque de mañana, yo había almorzado, y cuando ansí como algo, hágote saber que hasta la noche me estoy ansí.
t: "Well, I had breakfasted in the morning, and when I eat anything, let me tell you, I keep at it until nightfall."

o: Por eso, pásate como pudieres, que después cenaremos.
t: So, eat as best you can, for we shall have supper later on.

o: Vuestra merced crea, cuando esto le oí, que estuve en poco de caer de mi estado, no tanto de hambre como por conocer de todo en todo la fortuna serme adversa.
t: Your grace may believe, when he heard this, that I was close to falling from my state, not so much from hunger as from knowing beyond a doubt that fortune was adverse to me.

o: Allí se me representaron de nuevo mis fatigas, y torné a llorar mis trabajos; allí se me vino a la memoria la consideración que hacía cuando me pensaba ir del clérigo, diciendo que aunque aquél era desventurado y mísero, por ventura toparía con otro peor: finalmente, allí lloré mi trabajosa vida pasada y mi cercana muerte venidera.
t: There my labors were set before me anew, and I fell once more to weeping over my troubles; there it came back to me the reflection I had made when I thought of leaving the cleric, saying that though he was unfortunate and miserable, perhaps I should light upon another worse: in short, there I wept over my toilsome past life and my near and approaching death.

o: Y con todo, disimulando lo mejor que pude.
t: And all the same, I hid it as best I could.

o: "Señor, mozo soy que no me fatigo mucho por comer, bendito Dios.
t: "Sir, I am a lad and do not tire myself much with eating, blessed be God.

o: Deso me podré yo alabar entre todos mis iguales por de mejor garganta, y ansí fui yo loado della fasta hoy día de los amos que yo he tenido."
t: For that I may praise myself among all my fellows as having the best throat, and thus have I been praised for it up to this day by the masters I have had."

o: "Virtud es ésa -dijo él- y por eso te querré yo más, porque el hartar es de los puercos y el comer regladamente es de los hombres de bien."
t: "Virtue is that," said he, "and that is why I shall love you the more, for stuffing oneself is for pigs, and eating in moderation is for decent men."

o: "¡Bien te he entendido!
t: "I understand you well enough!

o: -dije yo entre mí- ¡maldita tanta medicina y bondad como aquestos mis amos que yo hallo hallan en la hambre!"
t: —I said to myself— cursed be so much medicine and kindness as these masters of mine, whom I find, find in the hunger!

o: Púseme a un cabo del portal y saqué unos pedazos de pan del seno, que me habían quedado de los de por Dios.
t: I took up a position at one end of the porch and pulled out some pieces of bread from my bosom, which had been left me from the leftovers.

o: Él, que vio esto, díjome.
t: He, who saw this, said to me:

o: "Ven acá, mozo. ¿Qué comes?"
t: "Come here, lad. What are you eating?"

o: Yo lleguéme a él y mostréle el pan.
t: I went up to him and showed him the bread.

o: Tomóme él un pedazo, de tres que eran el mejor y más grande, y díjome.
t: He took a piece from me, of the three that were the best and largest, and said to me:

o: "Por mi vida, que parece éste buen pan."
t: "By my life, this seems good bread."

o: "¡Y cómo! ¿Agora -dije yo-, señor, es bueno?"
t: "You can say that! Now," said I, "sir, is it good?"

o: ¿Adónde lo hubiste?
t: Where did you get it?

o: ¿Si es amasado de manos limpias?"
t: Is it kneaded with clean hands?

o: "No sé yo eso -le dije-; mas a mí no me pone asco el sabor dello."
t: "I don't know about that," I said, "but to me the taste of it doesn't turn my stomach."

o: "Así plega a Dios" -dijo el pobre de mi amo.
t: "God grant it so," said my poor master.

o: Y llevándolo a la boca, comenzó a dar en él tan fieros bocados como yo en lo otro.
t: And putting it to his mouth, he began to take such fierce bites of it as I did of the other.

o: "Sabrosísimo pan está -dijo-, por Dios."
t: "The bread is delicious," he said, "by God."

o: Y como le sentí de qué pie coxqueaba, dime priesa, porque le vi en disposición, si acababa antes que yo, se comediría a ayudarme a lo que me quedase; y con esto acabamos casi a una.
t: And since I saw which foot he limped on, I hurried, because I saw he was in such a mood that, if he finished before I did, he would spare himself the trouble of helping me with what was left for me; and with this we finished almost at one o'clock.

o: Y mi amo comenzó a sacudir con las manos unas pocas de migajas, y bien menudas, que en los pechos se le habían quedado, y entró en una camareta que allí estaba, y sacó un jarro desbocado y no muy nuevo, y desque hubo bebido convidóme con él.
t: And my master began shaking off with his hands a few crumbs, and very fine ones, that had stuck to his chest, and he went into a little room that was there, and brought out a jug with a chipped rim and not very new, and after he had drunk from it he invited me to drink with him.

o: Yo, por hacer del continente, dije.
t: I did so, to go along with the abstaining business.

o: "Señor, no bebo vino."
t: "Sir, I don't drink wine."

o: Bien puedes beber."
t: You may well drink."

o: Entonces tomé el jarro y bebí, no mucho, porque de sed no era mi congoja.
t: So I took the jug and drank, not much, because thirst was not my concern.

o: Ansí estuvimos hasta la noche, hablando en cosas que me preguntaba, a las cuales yo le respondí lo mejor que supe.
t: Thus we stayed until nightfall, talking about things he asked me about, which I answered as best I knew how.

o: En este tiempo metióme en la cámara donde estaba el jarro de que bebimos, y díjome.
t: In the meantime he took me into the room where the jug we had drunk from was, and said to me:

o: "Mozo, párate allí y verás, cómo hacemos esta cama, para que la sepas hacer de aquí adelante."
t: "Young man, stand there and watch how we make this bed, so that you may learn to make it from now on."

o: Púseme de un cabo y él del otro y hecimos la negra cama, en la cual no había mucho que hacer, porque ella tenía sobre unos bancos un cañizo, sobre el cual estaba tendida la ropa que, por no estar muy continuada a lavarse, no parecía colchón, aunque servía dél, con harta menos lana que era menester.
t: I stood at one end and he at the other, and we made the black bed, in which there was not much to do, because it had over some benches a wattle-work, on which was spread the bedding which, for not being washed often enough, did not look like a mattress, though it served as one, with far less wool than was needed.

o: Aquél tendimos, haciendo cuenta de ablandalle, lo cual era imposible, porque de lo duro mal se puede hacer blando.
t: We spread that on, counting on softening it, which was impossible, because what is hard cannot be made soft.

o: El diablo del enjalma maldita la cosa tenía dentro de sí, que puesto sobre el cañizo todas las cañas se señalaban y parecían a lo proprio entrecuesto de flaquísimo puerco; y sobre aquel hambriento colchón un alfamar del mesmo jaez, del cual el color yo no pude alcanzar.
t: The devil of the accursed wattle had the thing so full of itself that, laid upon the bed, every cane showed through and looked like the very lattice of a very lean hog; and on that hungry mattress an quilt of the same sort, whose color I could not make out.

o: Hecha la cama y la noche venida, díjome.
t: The bed made and night come, he said to me:

o: "Lázaro, ya es tarde, y de aquí a la plaza hay gran trecho.
t: "Lázaro, it is late now, and from here to the square is a good stretch.

o: También en esta ciudad andan muchos ladrones que siendo de noche capean.
t: There are many thieves about this city too, who are up to no good once night falls.

o: Pasemos como podamos y mañana, venido el día, Dios hará merced; porque yo, por estar solo, no estoy proveído, antes he comido estos días por allá fuera, mas agora hacerlo hemos de otra manera."
t: Let us get on as best we can, and tomorrow, when the day comes, God will provide; because I, being alone, am not stocked with food, for I have been eating these days out there, but now we must do it another way."

o: "Señor, de mí -dije yo- ninguna pena tenga vuestra merced, que sé pasar una noche y aun más, si es menester, sin comer."
t: "Sir," said I, "let your grace not trouble about me; I can manage a night, and even more, if need be, without eating."

o: "Vivirás más y más sano -me respondió-, porque como decíamos hoy, no hay tal cosa en el mundo para vivir mucho que comer poco."
t: "You will live longer and healthier," he answered me, "because, as we were saying today, there is nothing in the world better for living long than eating little."

o: "Si por esa vía es -dije entre mí-, nunca yo moriré, que siempre he guardado esa regla por fuerza, y aun espero en mi desdicha tenella toda mi vida."
t: "If that is the way," I said to myself, "I shall never die, for I have always kept to that rule by necessity, and I still hope, in my misfortune, to keep it all my life."

o: Y acostóse en la cama, poniendo por cabecera las calzas y el jubón, y mandóme echar a sus pies, lo cual yo hice; mas ¡maldito el sueño que yo dormí!
t: He lay down in the bed, using his breeches and doublet for a bolster, and told me to lie at his feet, which I did; but cursed be the sleep I slept!

o: Porque las cañas y mis salidos huesos en toda la noche dejaron de rifar y encenderse, que con mis trabajos, males y hambre, pienso que en mi cuerpo no había libra de carne; y también, como aquel día no había comido casi nada, rabiaba de hambre, la cual con el sueño no tenía amistad.
t: Because the canes and my protruding bones left off scraping and grating all night long, and with my labors, my pains and my hunger, I think there was not an ounce of flesh left in my body; and also, since that day I had scarcely eaten anything, I was rabbiding with hunger, which has no friendship with sleep.

o: Maldíjeme mil veces -¡Dios me lo perdone!- y a mi ruin fortuna, allí lo más de la noche, y (lo peor) no osándome revolver por no despertalle, pedí a Dios muchas veces la muerte.
t: I cursed him a thousand times—may God forgive me!—and my wretched fortune, there through most of the night, and (worst of all), not daring to turn over for fear of waking him, I begged God for death many times over.

o: La mañana venida, levantámonos, y comienza a limpiar y sacudir sus calzas y jubón y sayo y capa -y yo que le servía de pelillo- y vístese muy a su placer de espacio.
t: Morning came, we got up, and he began to brush and shake out his breeches and doublet and cloak and gown—and I who served him as his valet—and he dressed himself very much at his ease and leisure.

o: Echéle aguamanos, peinóse y puso su espada en el talabarte y, al tiempo que la ponía, díjome.
t: He poured water on his hands, combed his hair, and put his sword into its baldric, and as he was buckling it on, he said to me:

o: "¡Oh, si supieses, mozo, qué pieza es ésta!
t: "Oh, lad, if only you knew what a treasure this is!"

o: No hay marco de oro en el mundo por que yo la diese.
t: There is no golden frame in the world that I would part with it for.

o: Mas ansí ninguna de cuantas Antonio hizo, no acertó a ponelle los aceros tan prestos como ésta los tiene."
t: And yet, in this way, of all the swords Antonio ever made, none managed to set its steel edges as sharp as this one has."

o: Y sacóla de la vaina y tentóla con los dedos, diciendo.
t: And he drew it from the sheath and felt it with his fingers, saying:

o: Yo me obligo con ella cercenar un copo de lana."
t: I pledge myself to cut a lock of wool with it."

o: Y yo dije entre mí.
t: And I said to myself:

o: "Y yo con mis dientes, aunque no son de acero, un pan de cuatro libras."
t: "And I with my teeth, though they are not steel, a four-pound loaf of bread."

o: Tornóla a meter y ciñósela y un sartal de cuentas gruesas del talabarte, y con un paso sosegado y el cuerpo derecho, haciendo con él y con la cabeza muy gentiles meneos, echando el cabo de la capa sobre el hombro y a veces so el brazo, y poniendo la mano derecha en el costado, salió por la puerta, diciendo.
t: He sheathed it again, girded it on, and took a string of large beads from his baldric, and with a calm step and his body straight, making very genteel motions with it and with his head, throwing the end of his cloak over his shoulder and now and then under his arm, and setting his right hand on his hip, he went out through the door, saying:

o: "Lázaro, mira por la casa en tanto que voy a oír misa, y haz la cama, y ve por la vasija de agua al río, que aquí bajo está, y cierra la puerta con llave, no nos hurten algo, y ponla aquí al quicio, porque si yo viniere en tanto pueda entrar."
t: "Lazarillo, keep an eye on the house while I go to hear mass, and make the bed, and fetch the water jar from the river, which is down below, and lock the door, so that no one steals anything from us, and set the key here in the doorpost, so that if I come back in the meantime I can get in."

o: Y súbese por la calle arriba con tan gentil semblante y continente, que quien no le conociera pensara ser muy cercano pariente al conde de Arcos, o a lo menos camarero que le daba de vestir.
t: And he went up the street with so gentle a bearing and demeanor that anyone who did not know him would think him a very close relative of the Count of Arcos, or at least his valet who dressed him.

o: "¡Bendito seáis vos, Señor -quedé yo diciendo-, que dais la enfermedad y ponéis el remedio!
t: "Blessed be you, sir," I said, "for you give the sickness and provide the remedy!"

o: ¿Quién encontrara a aquel mi señor que no piense, según el contento de sí lleva, haber anoche bien cenado y dormido en buena cama, y aun agora es de mañana, no le cuenten por muy bien almorzado?
t: Who would find that my master, judging by the self-satisfaction he carries, does not think he supped well last night and slept in a good bed, and even now it is morning—let them not count him as having had a very good breakfast?

o: ¡Grandes secretos son, Señor, los que vos hacéis y las gentes ignoran!
t: Great secrets are those you are keeping, sir, that people know nothing of!

o: Nadie por cierto lo sospechara.
t: No one would certainly have suspected it.

o: ¡Oh Señor, y cuántos de aquéstos debéis vos tener por el mundo derramados, que padecen por la negra que llaman honra lo que por vos no sufrirían!"
t: "Oh sir, and how many of these you must have scattered about the world, who suffer for the black thing they call honor what they would not suffer for you!"

o: Ansí estaba yo a la puerta, mirando y considerando estas cosas y otras muchas, hasta que el señor mi amo traspuso la larga y angosta calle, y como lo vi trasponer, tornéme a entrar en casa, y en un credo la anduve toda, alto y bajo, sin hacer represa ni hallar en qué.
t: Thus I stood at the door, watching and pondering these things and many others, until my master crossed the long, narrow street; and as I saw him cross, I turned back into the house, and in a trice I walked it all over, high and low, without making a stop or finding anything.

o: Y como digo, él estaba entre ellas hecho un Macías, diciéndoles más dulzuras que Ovidio escribió.
t: And as I say, he was among them made up as a Macías, telling them more sweet things than Ovid ever wrote.

o: Pero como sintieron dél que estaba bien enternecido, no se les hizo de vergüenza pedirle de almorzar con el acostumbrado pago.
t: But since they felt he was well moved, they were not ashamed to ask him for breakfast with the customary payment.

o: Él, sintiéndose tan frío de bolsa cuanto estaba caliente del estómago, tomóle tal calofrío que le robó la color del gesto, y comenzó a turbarse en la plática y a poner excusas no validas.
t: He, feeling as cold in the purse as he was hot in the stomach, was seized by such a chill that it stole the color from his face, and he began to grow confused in his talk and to offer invalid excuses.

o: Ellas, que debían ser bien instituídas, como le sintieron la enfermedad, dejáronle para el que era.
t: They, who ought to have been well provided for, as soon as they felt his illness, left it to him who it belonged to.

o: Yo, que estaba comiendo ciertos tronchos de berzas, con los cuales me desayuné, con mucha diligencia, como mozo nuevo, sin ser visto de mi amo, torné a casa, de la cual pensé barrer alguna parte, que era bien menester, mas no hallé con qué.
t: I, who was eating certain stalks of cabbage, with which I had breakfasted very diligently, like a new servant, without being seen by my master, turned back toward home, of which I thought to sweep some part, which was badly needed, but I found nothing with which to do it.

o: Púseme a pensar qué haría, y parecióme esperar a mi amo hasta que el día demediase y si viniese y por ventura trajese algo que comiésemos; mas en vano fue mi experiencia.
t: I began to think what I should do, and it seemed best to wait for my master until the day was half over and, if he came, and by chance brought something for us to eat; but my waiting was in vain.

o: Desque vi ser las dos y no venía y la hambre me aquejaba, cierro mi puerta y pongo la llave do mandó, y tórnome a mi menester.
t: When I saw it was two o'clock and he was not coming and hunger was pressing me, I shut my door and set the key where he had ordered, and I turned to my task.

o: Con baja y enferma voz e inclinadas mis manos en los senos, puesto Dios ante mis ojos y la lengua en su nombre, comienzo a pedir pan por las puertas y casas más grandes que me parecía.
t: With a low and sickly voice and my hands folded upon my breast, with God before my eyes and my tongue in his name, I began to ask for bread at the doors and houses bigger than it seemed to me proper.

o: Volvíme a la posada y al pasar por la tripería pedí a una de aquellas mujeres, y diome un pedazo de uña de vaca con otras pocas de tripas cocidas.
t: I returned to the inn and, passing by the tripe shop, I asked one of those women, and she gave me a piece of cow's heel along with a few other pieces of boiled tripe.

o: Cuando llegué a casa, ya el bueno de mi amo estaba en ella, doblada su capa y puesta en el poyo, y él paseándose por el patio.
t: When I arrived home, my good master was already in it, his cloak folded and laid on the bench, and he himself strolling about the courtyard.

o: Como entro, vínose para mí.
t: As I came in, he came over to me.

o: Pensé que me quería reñir la tardanza, mas mejor lo hizo Dios.
t: I thought he meant to scold me for the delay, but God did better.

o: Preguntóme dó venía. Yo le dije.
t: He asked me where I came from. I told him.

o: "Señor, hasta que dio las dos estuve aquí, y de que vi que V.M. no venía, fuime por esa ciudad a encomendarme a las buenas gentes, y hanme dado esto que veis."
t: "Sir, until it struck two I was here, and when I saw that Your Grace was not coming, I went about the town to recommend myself to good people, and they have given me this that you see."

o: Mostréle el pan y las tripas que en un cabo de la halda traía, a lo cual él mostró buen semblante y dijo.
t: I showed him the bread and the tripe that I was carrying in the end of my skirt, at which he showed a good countenance and said:

o: "Pues esperado te he a comer, y de que vi que no veniste, comí.
t: "Well, I was expecting you to eat, and since I saw you were not coming, I ate."

o: Mas tú haces como hombre de bien en eso, que más vale pedillo por Dios que no hurtallo, y ansí Él me ayude como ello me parece bien.
t: But you act like an honest man in that, for it is better to beg it of God than to steal it, and so may He help me as it seems right to me.

o: Y solamente te encomiendo no sepan que vives comigo, por lo que toca a mi honra, aunque bien creo que será secreto, según lo poco que en este pueblo soy conocido.
t: And I only ask you that they not learn you live with me, as concerns my honor, though I well believe it will be a secret, since I am so little known in this town.

o: ¡Nunca a él yo hubiera de venir!"
t: "I would never have come to him!"

o: "De eso pierda, señor, cuidado -le dije yo-, que maldito aquél que ninguno tiene de pedirme esa cuenta ni yo de dalla."
t: "Let him worry about that, sir," I told him, "for cursed is he who has no business asking me for that account, nor I of giving it."

o: "Agora pues, come, pecador.
t: "Now then, eat, you sinner."

o: Que, si a Dios place, presto nos veremos sin necesidad; aunque te digo que después que en esta casa entré, nunca bien me ha ido.
t: For, if God pleases, we shall soon meet without need of it; though I tell you that since I entered this house, things have never gone well with me.

o: Debe ser de mal suelo, que hay casas desdichadas y de mal pie, que a los que viven en ellas pegan la desdicha.
t: It must be an unlucky spot, for there are unfortunate houses and houses of ill footing, and misfortune sticks to those who live in them.

o: Ésta debe de ser sin dubda de ellas; mas yo te prometo, acabado el mes, no quede en ella aunque me la den por mía."
t: "This must be one of them without a doubt; but I promise you, by the end of the month, there will be nothing left of it, even if they hand it over to me as mine."

o: Sentéme al cabo del poyo y, porque no me tuviese por glotón, callé la merienda; y comienzo a cenar y morder en mis tripas y pan, y disimuladamente miraba al desventurado señor mío, que no partía sus ojos de mis faldas, que aquella sazón servían de plato.
t: I sat down at the end of the bench and, so that I might not be taken for a glutton, held back from the afternoon snack; and I began to eat, chewing on my innards and bread, and stealthily I watched my wretched master, who never took his eyes off my skirts, which at that moment served him as a plate.

o: Tanta lástima haya Dios de mí como yo había dél, porque sentí lo que sentía, y muchas veces había por ello pasado y pasaba cada día.
t: May God have as much pity on me as I had on him, because I felt what he felt, and many times I had suffered from it and suffered from it every day.

o: Pensaba si sería bien comedirme a convidalle; mas por me haber dicho que había comido, temía me no aceptaría el convite.
t: I was thinking whether it would be good for me to invite him to eat with me; but since he had told me he had already eaten, I feared he would not accept my invitation.

o: Finalmente, yo deseaba aquel pecador ayudase a su trabajo del mío, y se desayunase como el día antes hizo, pues había mejor aparejo, por ser mejor la vianda y menos mi hambre.
t: In short, I wanted that sinner to help me with his task of feeding me, and to breakfast as he had done the day before, for there was better provision, since the food was better and my hunger less.

o: Quiso Dios cumplir mi deseo, y aun pienso que el suyo, porque, como comencé a comer y él se andaba paseando llegóse a mí y díjome.
t: God willed to grant my desire, and I even think He granted his own, because, as I began to eat and he was strolling about, he came up to me and said to me:

o: "Dígote, Lázaro, que tienes en comer la mejor gracia que en mi vida vi a hombre, y que nadie te lo verá hacer que no le pongas gana aunque no la tenga."
t: "I tell you, Lázaro, you have the finest grace at eating that I have ever seen in a man, and nobody will see you do it without being made to want it, even if he has no appetite."

o: "La muy buena que tú tienes -dije yo entre mí- te hace parecer la mía hermosa."
t: "The very good grace you have," I said to myself, "makes mine look beautiful."

o: Con todo, parecióme ayudarle, pues se ayudaba y me abría camino para ello, y díjele.
t: All the same, it seemed to me that I was helping him, for he was helping himself and clearing the way for it, and I said to him:

o: "Señor, el buen aparejo hace buen artífice.
t: "Sir, good provision makes a good craftsman.

o: Este pan está sabrosísimo y esta uña de vaca tan bien cocida y sazonada, que no habrá a quien no convide con su sabor."
t: "This bread is wonderfully tasty, and this cow's heel so well cooked and seasoned that there will be no one it does not invite with its flavor."

o: "Dígote que es el mejor bocado del mundo, que no hay faisán que ansí me sepa."
t: "I tell you it is the best morsel in the world; there is no pheasant that tastes so good to me."

o: "Pues pruebe, señor, y verá qué tal está."
t: "Well, try it, sir, and see how it is."

o: Póngole en las uñas la otra y tres o cuatro raciones de pan de lo más blanco y asentóseme al lado, y comienza a comer como aquel que lo había gana, royendo cada huesecillo de aquéllos mejor que un galgo suyo lo hiciera.
t: I put the other heel on his fingers and three or four slices of the whitest bread, and sat down beside him, and he began to eat like a man who had an appetite for it, gnawing every little bone of those better than any greyhound of his would have done.

o: "Con almodrote -decía- es éste singular manjar."
t: "With almond paste," he said, "this is a singular dish."

o: "Con mejor salsa lo comes tú", respondí yo paso.
t: "You eat it with a better sauce," I answered slowly.

o: "Por Dios, que me ha sabido como si hoy no hobiera comido bocado."
t: "By God, it has tasted to me as if I had not eaten a bite today."

o: "¡Ansí me vengan los buenos años como es ello!"
t: "May the good years come to me just like this!"

o: -dije yo entre mí.
t: "—I said to myself.

o: Pidióme el jarro del agua y díselo como lo había traído.
t: He asked me for the water jug and I gave it to him as I had brought it.

o: Es señal que, pues no le faltaba el agua, que no le había a mi amo sobrado la comida.
t: It is a sign that, since water was not lacking, my master had not had food to spare.

o: Bebimos, y muy contentos nos fuimos a dormir como la noche pasada.
t: We drank, and very contentedly we went off to sleep as we had the night before.

o: Y por evitar prolijidad, desta manera estuvimos ocho o diez días, yéndose el pecador en la mañana con aquel contento y paso contado a papar aire por las calles, teniendo en el pobre Lázaro una cabeza de lobo.
t: And to avoid prolixity, in this manner we stayed eight or ten days, the sinner going out in the morning with that contentment and quiet tread to snap up air through the streets, with poor Lázaro having a wolf's head.

o: Contemplaba yo muchas veces mi desastre, que escapando de los amos ruines que había tenido y buscando mejoría, viniese a topar con quien no solo no me mantuviese, mas a quien yo había de mantener.
t: I often contemplated my misfortune: that, fleeing from the wicked masters I had had and seeking a better lot, I should run into one who not only would not support me, but whom I would have to support.

o: Con todo, le quería bien, con ver que no tenía ni podía más, y antes le había lástima que enemistad; y muchas veces, por llevar a la posada con que él lo pasase, yo lo pasaba mal.
t: Withal, I loved him well, seeing that he had nothing and could have no more, and I felt more pity for him than enmity; and many times, to bring him to the inn with what would let him get through the day, I myself went hungry.

o: Porque una mañana, levantándose el triste en camisa, subió a lo alto de la casa a hacer sus menesteres, y en tanto yo, por salir de sospecha, desenvolvíle el jubón y las calzas que a la cabecera dejó, y hallé una bolsilla de terciopelo raso hecho cien dobleces y sin maldita la blanca ni señal que la hobiese tenido mucho tiempo.
t: Because one morning, the sad man getting up in his shirt, climbed to the top of the house to do his chores, and meanwhile I, to get out of suspicion, took out the doublet and breeches he had left at the head of the bed, and found a little pocket of smooth velvet folded a hundred times over and not a whit of white nor any sign that it had been there long.

o: "Éste -decía yo- es pobre y nadie da lo que no tiene.
t: "This one," I said, "is poor, and nobody gives what he does not have."

o: Mas el avariento ciego y el malaventurado mezquino clérigo que, con dárselo Dios a ambos, al uno de mano besada y al otro de lengua suelta, me mataban de hambre, aquéllos es justo desamar y aquéste de haber mancilla."
t: But the blind miser and the unfortunate mean-spirited cleric who, if God gave it to them both, the one with the soft hand and the other with the loose tongue, were killing me with hunger: those it is just to stop loving, and this one for having stained his hands."

o: Dios es testigo que hoy día, cuando topo con alguno de su hábito, con aquel paso y pompa, le he lástima, con pensar si padece lo que aquél le vi sufrir; al cual con toda su pobreza holgaría de servir más que a los otros por lo que he dicho.
t: God is witness that today, when I run into one of his kidney, with that step and pomp, I feel sorry for him, thinking whether he suffers what I saw him suffer; and in all his poverty I would gladly serve him more than the others, for what I have said.

o: Sólo tenía dél un poco de descontento: que quisiera yo me no tuviera tanta presunción, mas que abajara un poco su fantasía con lo mucho que subía su necesidad.
t: Only I was a little discontented with him: I wished he did not have so much conceit, but that he would lower his fancy a bit, seeing how high his need rose.

o: Mas, según me parece, es regla ya entre ellos usada y guardada; aunque no haya cornado de trueco, ha de andar el birrete en su lugar.
t: But, as it seems to me, it is a rule already used and kept among them; though there be no genuine horn, the cap must still go in its place.

o: El Señor lo remedie, que ya con este mal han de morir.
t: The Lord remedy it, for with this ill they must already die.

o: Pues, estando yo en tal estado, pasando la vida que digo, quiso mi mala fortuna, que de perseguirme no era satisfecha, que en aquella trabajada y vergonzosa vivienda no durase.
t: Well, being in such a state, passing the life I have described, my bad luck willed that, not satisfied with persecuting me, it should not last in that toilsome and shameful dwelling.

o: Y fue, como el año en esta tierra fuese estéril de pan, acordaron el Ayuntamiento que todos los pobres estranjeros se fuesen de la ciudad, con pregón que el que de allí adelante topasen fuese punido con azotes.
t: And it was, since that year the land was barren of bread, that the City Council agreed that all poor strangers should leave the city, with a proclamation that whoever was found there afterward would be punished with lashes.

o: Y así, ejecutando la ley, desde a cuatro días que el pregón se dio, vi llevar una procesión de pobres azotando por las Cuatro Calles, lo cual me puso tan gran espanto, que nunca osé desmandarme a demandar.
t: And so, carrying out the law, four days after the proclamation was issued, I saw a procession of the poor being whipped through the Four Streets, which put such great fear into me that I never dared to go too far in demanding anything.

o: Aquí viera, quien vello pudiera, la abstinencia de mi casa y la tristeza y silencio de los moradores, tanto que nos acaeció estar dos o tres días sin comer bocado, ni hablaba palabra.
t: Here one would see, whoever had eyes to see, the abstinence of my house and the sadness and silence of the inhabitants, so that it befell us to go two or three days without eating a bite, nor speaking a word.

o: A mí diéronme la vida unas mujercillas hilanderas de algodón, que hacían bonetes y vivían par de nosotros, con las cuales yo tuve vecindad y conocimiento; que de la laceria que les traían me daban alguna cosilla, con la cual muy pasado me pasaba.
t: To me they gave life, some little cotton-spinning women who made caps and lived paired off with us, with whom I had neighborhood and acquaintance; from the scraps they brought me they gave me a little something, with which I got on very well.

o: Y no tenía tanta lástima de mí como del lastimado de mi amo, que en ocho días maldito el bocado que comió.
t: And I had not so much pity for myself as for my pitied master, who in eight days did not eat a cursed bite.

o: A lo menos, en casa bien lo estuvimos sin comer.
t: At least, at home we did well without eating.

o: No sé yo cómo o dónde andaba y qué comía.
t: I do not know how or where he was, or what he ate.

o: ¡Y velle venir a mediodía la calle abajo con estirado cuerpo, más largo que galgo de buena casta!
t: And see him coming down the street at noon with a stretched-out body, longer than a well-bred greyhound!

o: Y por lo que toca a su negra que dicen honra, tomaba una paja de las que aun asaz no había en casa, y salía a la puerta escarbando los dientes que nada entre sí tenían, quejándose todavía de aquel mal solar diciendo.
t: And as for his black one, which they call honor, he would take a straw from the few there still were in the house, and go out to the door picking his teeth, which had nothing at all between them, still complaining of that bad lodging, saying:

o: "Malo está de ver, que la desdicha desta vivienda lo hace.
t: "It is truly bad, that the misfortune of this dwelling makes it so.

o: Como ves, es lóbrega, triste, obscura.
t: As you see, it is gloomy, sad, dark.

o: Mientras aquí estuviéremos, hemos de padecer.
t: As long as we are here, we must suffer.

o: Ya deseo que se acabe este mes por salir della."
t: I already long for this month to end so I can get out of it."

o: Pues, estando en esta afligida y hambrienta persecución un día, no sé por cual dicha o ventura, en el pobre poder de mi amo entró un real, con el cual él vino a casa tan ufano como si tuviera el tesoro de Venecia; y con gesto muy alegre y risueño me lo dio, diciendo.
t: Well, one day, while we were in this afflicted and hungry strait, I know not by what luck or fortune, a real came into my master's poor hands, and with it he came home as proud as if he held the treasure of Venice; and with a very cheerful, smiling gesture he gave it to me, saying:

o: "Toma, Lázaro, que Dios ya va abriendo su mano.
t: "Take it, Lázaro, for God is already opening his hand.

o: Ve a la plaza y merca pan y vino y carne: ¡quebremos el ojo al diablo!
t: Go to the square and buy bread, wine and meat: let us blind the devil!

o: Y más, te hago saber, porque te huelgues, que he alquilado otra casa, y en ésta desastrada no hemos de estar más de en cumplimiento el mes.
t: And further, I tell you, so that you may enjoy yourself, I have rented another house, and in this wretched one we shall stay no longer than the month requires.

o: ¡Maldita sea ella y el que en ella puso la primera teja, que con mal en ella entré!
t: Cursed be it, and cursed be whoever laid the first tile on it, for I came into it ill!

o: Por Nuestro Señor, cuanto ha que en ella vivo, gota de vino ni bocado de carne no he comido, ni he habido descanso ninguno; mas ¡tal vista tiene y tal obscuridad y tristeza!
t: By Our Lord, all the time I have lived in it I have eaten not a drop of wine nor a bite of meat, nor had any rest at all; and what a view it has, what darkness and what sadness!

o: Ve y ven presto, y comamos hoy como condes."
t: Go, come quickly, and let us eat today like counts."

o: Tomo mi real y jarro y a los pies dándoles priesa, comienzo a subir mi calle encaminando mis pasos para la plaza muy contento y alegre.
t: I take my coin and my jug and, setting my feet a-going, I begin to climb my street, heading my steps toward the square, very content and happy.

o: Mas ¿qué me aprovecha si está constituido en mi triste fortuna que ningún gozo me venga sin zozobra?
t: But what good is it to me, if it is ordained in my unhappy fate that no joy comes to me without anxiety?

o: Y ansí fue éste; porque yendo la calle arriba, echando mi cuenta en lo que le emplearía que fuese mejor y más provechosamente gastado, dando infinitas gracias a Dios que a mi amo había hecho con dinero, a deshora me vino al encuentro un muerto, que por la calle abajo muchos clérigos y gente en unas andas traían.
t: And so it happened; for going up the street, reckoning how he might spend it better and more profitably, giving infinite thanks to God, who had put money in my master's hands, off hours a dead man came toward me, whom many clerics and folk were carrying down the street on a bier.

o: Arriméme a la pared por darles lugar, y desque el cuerpo pasó, venían luego a par del lecho una que debía ser mujer del difunto, cargada de luto, y con ella otras muchas mujeres; la cual iba llorando a grandes voces y diciendo.
t: I pressed myself against the wall to give them room, and once the body had passed, there came then beside the bier one who must have been the dead man's wife, clad in mourning, and with her many other women; she went weeping aloud and saying:

o: "Marido y señor mío, ¿adónde os me llevan?
t: "My husband and my lord, where are you taking me?

o: ¡A la casa triste y desdichada, a la casa lóbrega y obscura, a la casa donde nunca comen ni beben!"
t: To the sad and wretched house, to the gloomy and dark house, to the house where they never eat nor drink!"

o: Yo que aquello oí, juntóseme el cielo con la tierra, y dije.
t: When I heard that, heaven and earth came together in me, and I said.

o: "¡Oh desdichado de mí!
t: "Oh, wretched me!

o: Para mi casa llevan este muerto."
t: They're taking this dead man to my house."

o: Dejo el camino que llevaba y hendí por medio de la gente, y vuelvo por la calle abajo a todo el más correr que pude para mi casa, y entrando en ella cierro a grande priesa, invocando el auxilio y favor de mi amo, abrazándome dél, que me venga a ayudar y a defender la entrada.
t: I left the road I was on and pushed through the middle of the crowd, and went back down the street as fast as I could run toward my house, and going in I shut the door in great haste, calling on my master's help and favor, embracing him, to come and help me and defend the entrance.

o: El cual algo alterado, pensando que fuese otra cosa, me dijo.
t: He, somewhat disturbed, thinking it was something else, said to me:

o: "¿Qué es eso, mozo?
t: "What is that, lad?

o: ¿Qué has? ¿Por qué cierras la puerta con tal furia?"
t: What's wrong? Why are you shutting the door with such fury?

o: "¡Oh señor -dije yo- acuda aquí, que nos traen acá un muerto!"
t: "Oh, sir," I said, "come here, for they've brought us a dead man!"

o: "¿Cómo así?", respondió él.
t: "How so?" he replied.

o: "Aquí arriba lo encontré, y venía diciendo su mujer: "Marido y señor mio, ¿adónde os llevan?
t: "I found him up here, and he was saying as he came: 'Husband and master of mine, where are they taking you?

o: ¡A la casa lóbrega y obscura, a la casa triste y desdichada, a la casa donde nunca comen ni beben!
t: To the dreary and dark house, to the sad and wretched house, to the house where no one ever eats or drinks!

o: Acá, señor, nos le traen."
t: Here, sir, they're bringing him to us."

o: Y ciertamente, cuando mi amo esto oyó, aunque no tenía por qué estar muy risueño, rio tanto que muy gran rato estuvo sin poder hablar.
t: And truly, when my master heard this, though he had no cause to be very merry, he laughed so much that for a long while he could not speak.

o: En este tiempo tenía ya yo echada la aldaba a la puerta y puesto el hombro en ella por más defensa.
t: By this time I had already set the door knocker going and put my shoulder against the door for greater security.

o: Pasó la gente con su muerto, y yo todavía me recelaba que nos le habían de meter en casa; y después fue ya más harto de reír que de comer, el bueno de mi amo díjome.
t: The crowd passed on with its dead man, and I was still afraid they would force him on us into the house; and afterwards my good master was more given to laughing than to eating, he told me.

o: "Verdad es, Lázaro; según la viuda lo va diciendo, tú tuviste razón de pensar lo que pensaste.
t: "It's true, Lázaro; judging by what the widow says, you were right in what you thought.

o: Mas, pues Dios lo ha hecho mejor y pasan adelante, abre, abre, y ve por de comer."
t: But since God has arranged it better and they are moving on, open, open, and go and get us something to eat."

o: "Dejálos, señor, acaben de pasar la calle", dije yo.
t: "Let them be, sir, let them finish crossing the street," I said.

o: Al fin vino mi amo a la puerta de la calle, y ábrela esforzándome, que bien era menester, según el miedo y alteración, y me torno a encaminar.
t: At last my master came to the street door, and opening it with effort, urging me, for it was indeed necessary, given my fear and agitation, and I set out again on my way.

o: Mas aunque comimos bien aquel día, maldito el gusto yo tomaba en ello, ni en aquellos tres días torné en mi color; y mi amo muy risueño todas las veces que se le acordaba aquella mi cosideración.
t: But though we ate well that day, I enjoyed it not at all, nor did I regain my color in those three days; and my master, very merry, whenever he recalled that thought of mine.

o: De esta manera estuve con mi tercero y pobre amo, que fue este escudero, algunos días, y en todos deseando saber la intención de su venida y estada en esta tierra; porque desde el primer día que con él asenté, le conocí ser estranjero, por el poco conocimiento y trato que con los naturales della tenía.
t: Thus I stayed with my third and poor master, who was this squire, for some days, and all the while longing to know the purpose of his coming and stay in this land; because from the first day I settled with him, I knew him to be a foreigner, from the little acquaintance and dealings he had with the natives of it.

o: Al fin se cumplió mi deseo y supe lo que deseaba; porque un día que habíamos comido razonablemente y estaba algo contento, contóme su hacienda y díjome ser de Castilla la Vieja, y que había dejado su tierra no más de por no quitar el bonete a un caballero su vecino.
t: At last my wish was fulfilled and I learned what I had longed for; for one day, having eaten reasonably well and being in somewhat good humor, he told me of his estate and said he was from Old Castile, and that he had left his homeland only because he would not doff his cap to a gentleman, his neighbor.

o: "Señor -dije yo- si él era lo que decís y tenía más que vos, ¿no errábades en no quitárselo primero, pues decís que él también os lo quitaba?"
t: "Sir," said I, "if he is what you say and has more than you, were you not wrong not to doff it to him first, since you say he also doffed it to you?"

o: "Sí es, y sí tiene, y también me lo quitaba él a mí; mas, de cuantas veces yo se le quitaba primero, no fuera malo comedirse él alguna y ganarme por la mano."
t: "Yes, he is, and yes, he has, and he did doff it to me as well; but of all the times I doffed mine to him first, it would not have been bad for him to return the favor and outdo me."

o: "Paréceme, señor -le dije yo- que en eso no mirara, mayormente con mis mayores que yo y que tienen más."
t: "It seems to me, sir," said I, "that in that you did not consider, especially with those older than I and who have more."

o: "Eres mochacho -me respondió- y no sientes las cosas de la honra, en que el día de hoy está todo el caudal de los hombres de bien.
t: "You are a lad," he answered me, "and you do not feel the things of honor, in which today all the wealth of good men lies."

o: Pues te hago saber que yo soy, como vees, un escudero; mas ¡vótote a Dios!, si al conde topo en la calle y no me quita muy bien quitado del todo el bonete, que otra vez que venga, me sepa yo entrar en una casa, fingiendo yo en ella algún negocio, o atravesar otra calle, si la hay, antes que llegue a mí, por no quitárselo.
t: So you must know that I am, as you see, a squire; but, God bless you, if I meet the count in the street and he does not take off his cap to me quite properly, entirely off, then the next time he comes, let me know I can enter a house, pretending I have some business there, or cross another street, if there is one, before he reaches me, so as not to doff it to him.

o: Que un hidalgo no debe a otro que a Dios y al rey nada, ni es justo, siendo hombre de bien, se descuide un punto de tener en mucho su persona.
t: For a gentleman owes nothing to anyone but God and the king, nor is it just, being a man of honor, to be careless in the least in keeping his person highly regarded.

o: Acuérdome que un día deshonré en mi tierra a un oficial, y quise ponerle las manos, porque cada vez que le topaba me decía: «Mantenga Dios a vuestra merced.»
t: I remember that one day I disgraced an officer in my town, and I wanted to lay hands on him, because every time I met him he said to me, "May God keep your grace."

o: «Vos, don villano ruin -le dije yo- ¿por qué no sois bien criado?
t: "You, base villain," said I, "why are you not well bred?"

o: ¿Manténgaos Dios, me habéis de decir, como si fuese quienquiera?»
t: "May God keep you, you must say, as if you were anybody?"

o: De allí adelante, de aquí acullá, me quitaba el bonete y hablaba como debía."
t: From then on, from that point on, I would take off my cap and speak as I ought.

o: "¿Y no es buena manera de saludar un hombre a otro -dije yo- decirle que le mantenga Dios?"
t: "And isn't it a good way for one man to greet another," said I, "to tell him may God keep him?"

o: "¡Mira mucho de enhoramala!
t: "Look how much "God keep you" they say!

o: -dijo él-. A los hombres de poca arte dicen eso, mas a los más altos, como yo, no les han de hablar menos de: «Beso las manos de vuestra merced», o por lo menos: «Bésoos, señor, las manos», si el que me habla es caballero.
t: said he. "To men of low estate they say that, but to the highest, like me, they must say no less than: "I kiss the hands of your lordship," or at least: "I kiss your hands, sir," if the one who speaks to me is a gentleman.

o: Y ansí, de aquél de mi tierra que me atestaba de mantenimiento nunca más le quise sufrir, ni sufriría ni sufriré a hombre del mundo, del rey abajo, que «Manténgaos Dios» me diga."
t: And so, from that man of my land who provided for my upkeep, I never again was willing to put up with it, nor would I, nor will I, as long as I live, allow any man in the world, from the king downward, to say to me "May God keep you."

o: "Pecador de mí -dije yo-, por eso tiene tan poco cuidado de mantenerte, pues no sufres que nadie se lo ruegue."
t: "Sinner me," said I, "that is why he takes so little care to keep you, since you don't let anyone ask it of him."

o: Y vine a esta ciudad, pensando que hallaría un buen asiento, mas no me ha sucedido como pensé.
t: And I came to this city, thinking I would find a good position, but it has not turned out as I thought.

o: Canónigos y señores de la iglesia, muchos hallo, mas es gente tan limitada que no los sacaran de su paso todo el mundo.
t: Canonicals and church lords, I find many, but they are such limited folk that the whole world could not drag them out of their rut.

o: Caballeros de media talla, también me ruegan; mas servir con éstos es gran trabajo, porque de hombre os habéis de convertir en malilla y si no.
t: Half-baked gentlemen also importune me; but serving these is hard work, because you have to turn yourself into a scoundrel, or else.

o: «Andá con Dios» os dicen.
t: "Go with God," they tell you.

o: Y las más veces son los pagamentos a largos plazos, y las más y las más ciertas, comido por servido.
t: And most often the payments come on long terms, and the surest and most certain of them, eaten alive for all the service rendered.

o: Ya cuando quieren reformar conciencia y satisfaceros vuestros sudores, sois librados en la recámara, en un sudado jubón o raída capa o sayo.
t: When they want to reform their conscience and make good on your sweat, you are let off in the garret, in a sweaty doublet or a threadbare cloak or coat.

o: Ya cuando asienta un hombre con un señor de título, todavía pasa su laceria.
t: When a man settles in with a lord of title, his lowness still shows through.

o: ¿Pues por ventura no hay en mi habilidad para servir y contestar a éstos?
t: Is it perhaps not within my ability to serve and answer these men?

o: Y a los señores dél parecen bien, y no quieren ver en sus casas hombres virtuosos, antes los aborrecen y tienen en poco y llaman necios y que no son personas de negocios ni con quien el señor se puede descuidar.
t: And to those lords they seem good, and they do not want to see virtuous men in their houses; rather they abhor them and hold them in little, calling them fools, and say they are not men of business, nor anyone with whom the master can afford to be careless.

o: Y con éstos los astutos usan, como digo, el día de hoy, de lo que yo usaría.
t: And with these the cunning men use, as I say, today what I would use.

o: Mas no quiere mi ventura que le halle."
t: But my good fortune does not will that I find him."

o: Desta manera lamentaba también su adversa fortuna mi amo, dándome relación de su persona valerosa.
t: In this way my master also lamented his adverse fortune, giving me an account of his valorous person.

o: Pues, estando en esto, entró por la puerta un hombre y una vieja.
t: Now, while this was going on, a man and an old woman came in through the door.

o: El hombre le pide el alquiler de la casa y la vieja el de la cama.
t: The man asks him for the rent of the house, and the old woman for the bed's.

o: Hacen cuenta, y de dos en dos meses le alcanzaron lo que él en un año no alcanzara: pienso que fueron doce o trece reales.
t: They do the reckoning, and every two months they collect what he would not have reached in a year: I think it was twelve or thirteen reales.

o: Y él les dio muy buena respuesta: que saldría a la plaza a trocar una pieza de a dos, y que a la tarde volviese.
t: And he gave them a very good answer: that he would go out to the square to exchange a two-real piece, and would come back in the afternoon.

o: Mas su salida fue sin vuelta.
t: But his going out was without a return.

o: Por manera que a la tarde ellos volvieron, mas fue tarde.
t: So that in the afternoon they came back, but it was late.

o: Yo les dije que aún no era venido.
t: I told them he had not yet come back.

o: Venida la noche, y él no, yo hube miedo de quedar en casa solo, y fuime a las vecinas y contéles el caso, y allí dormí.
t: Night came, and he did not, and I was afraid of being left alone in the house, so I went to the neighbors' and told them the whole story, and there I slept.

o: Venida la mañana, los acreedores vuelven y preguntan por el vecino, mas a estotra puerta.
t: Morning came, the creditors returned and asked for the neighbor, but at the other door.

o: Las mujeres le responden: "Veis aquí su mozo y la llave de la puerta."
t: The women answer them: "Here is his servant and the key to the door."

o: Ellos me préguntaron por él y díjele que no sabía adónde estaba y que tampoco había vuelto a casa desde que salió a trocar la pieza, y que pensaba que de mí y de ellos se había ido con el trueco.
t: They asked me about him, and I told them I did not know where he was, nor that he had come back to the house since he went out to exchange the piece, and that I thought he had gone off with the money from the exchange.

o: De que esto me oyeron, van por un alguacil y un escribano.
t: When they heard this, they went for a constable and a notary.

o: Y helos do vuelven luego con ellos, y toman la llave, y llámanme, y llaman testigos, y abren la puerta, y entran a embargar la hacienda de mi amo hasta ser pagados de su deuda.
t: And there they were again with them, and they took the key, and called me, and called witnesses, and opened the door, and entered to seize my master's property until they were paid their debt.

o: Anduvieron toda la casa y halláronla desembarazada, como he contado, y dícenme.
t: They searched the whole house and found it cleared out, as I have told, and they say to me.

o: "¿Qué es de la hacienda de tu amo, sus arcas y paños de pared y alhajas de casa?"
t: "What has become of your master's property, his chests and wall hangings and household furnishings?"

o: "No sé yo eso", le respondí.
t: "I don't know that," I answered him.

o: "Sin duda -dicen ellos- esta noche lo deben de haber alzado y llevado a alguna parte.
t: "No doubt," say they, "they must have moved it last night and carried it off somewhere."

o: Señor alguacil, prended a este mozo, que él sabe dónde está."
t: "Sir constable, arrest this lad, for he knows where it is."

o: En esto vino el alguacil, y echóme mano por el collar del jubón, diciendo.
t: At this the constable came and laid hold of me by the collar of my doublet, saying.

o: "Mochacho, tú eres preso si no descubres los bienes deste tu amo."
t: "Young man, you are under arrest unless you reveal the goods of your master."

o: Yo, como en otra tal no me hubiese visto -porque asido del collar, sí, había sido muchas e infinitas veces, mas era mansamente dél trabado, para que mostrase el camino al que no vía- yo hube mucho miedo, y llorando prometíle de decir lo que preguntaban.
t: I, who had never seen myself in another such plight—for I had indeed been seized by the collar many and infinite times, but he held it gently, so that I might show the way to what I had not seen—was much afraid, and weeping I promised to tell them what they asked.

o: "Bien está -dicen ellos-, pues di todo lo que sabes, y no hayas temor."
t: "Very well," say they, "then tell all you know, and have no fear."

o: Sentóse el escribano en un poyo para escrebir el inventario, preguntándome qué tenía.
t: The clerk sat down on a bench to write out the inventory, asking me what he had.

o: "Señores -dije yo-, lo que este mi amo tiene, según él me dijo, es un muy buen solar de casas y un palomar derribado."
t: "Gentlemen," I said, "what this master of mine has, as he told me, is a very good site of houses and a dovecote fallen in."

o: "Bien está -dicen ellos-.
t: "Very well," say they.

o: Por poco que eso valga, hay para nos entregar de la deuda.
t: However little that may be worth, there is enough to pay us off the debt.

o: ¿Y a qué parte de la ciudad tiene eso?", me preguntaron.
t: "And in what part of the city does he have that?" they asked me.

o: "En su tierra", respondí.
t: "In his lands," I answered.

o: "Por Dios, que está bueno el negocio -dijeron ellos-.
t: "By God, this is a good piece of business," they said.

o: ¿Y adónde es su tierra?"
t: "And where are his lands?"

o: "De Castilla la Vieja me dijo él que era", le dije yo.
t: "He told me they were in Old Castile," I told him.

o: Riéronse mucho el alguacil y el escribano, diciendo.
t: The constable and the clerk laughed a great deal, saying.

o: "Bastante relación es ésta para cobrar vuestra deuda, aunque mejor fuese."
t: "This is quite enough to pay your debt, though it would be better still."

o: Las vecinas, que estaban presentes, dijeron.
t: The neighbors who were present said so.

o: "Señores, éste es un niño inocente, y ha pocos días que está con ese escudero, y no sabe dél más que vuestras merecedes, sino cuánto el pecadorcico se llega aquí a nuestra casa, y le damos de comer lo que podemos por amor de Dios, y a las noches se iba a dormir con él."
t: "Gentlemen, this is an innocent boy, and it is only a few days since he has been with that squire, and he knows nothing of him beyond what your worships know, except how the little sinner comes here to our house, and we give him what food we can for the love of God, and at night he would go off to sleep with him."

o: Vista mi inocencia, dejáronme, dándome por libre.
t: Seeing my innocence, they let me go, granting me my freedom.

o: Y el alguacil y el escribano piden al hombre y a la mujer sus derechos, sobre lo cual tuvieron gran contienda y ruido, porque ellos alegaron no ser obligados a pagar, pues no había de qué ni se hacía el embargo.
t: And the constable and the clerk asked the man and the woman for their fees, over which there was a great dispute and uproar, because they argued they were not obliged to pay, since there was nothing to seize and no seizure was made.

o: Los otros decían que habían dejado de ir a otro negocio que les importaba más por venir a aquél.
t: The others said they had given up going to another business that mattered more to them, to come to this one.

o: Finalmente, después de dadas muchas voces, al cabo carga un porquerón con el viejo alfamar de la vieja, aunque no iba muy cargado.
t: Finally, after much shouting, at last a swineherd loaded up with the old saddle of the old woman, though he was not carrying it very heavy.

o: Allá van todos cinco dando voces.
t: There they all go, all five of them, shouting.

o: No sé en qué paró.
t: I don't know how it ended.

o: Creo yo que el pecador alfamar pagara por todos, y bien se empleaba, pues el tiempo que había de reposar y descansar de los trabajos pasados, se andaba alquilando.
t: I think the wretched saddle paid for everyone, and it was well spent, for the time he had to rest and take a breath after past labors was spent being rented out.

o: Así, como he contado, me dejó mi pobre tercero amo, do acabé de conocer mi ruin dicha, pues, señalándose todo lo que podría contra mí, hacía mis negocios tan al revés, que los amos, que suelen ser dejados de los mozos, en mí no fuese ansí, mas que mi amo me dejase y huyese de mí.
t: So, as I have told, my poor third master left me, where I came to know my wretched fate, for, pointing out everything that could be done against me, he turned my affairs so upside down that the masters, who are usually abandoned by their servants, in my case it was not so, but rather that my master should leave me and flee from me.
